case.title: Knoevenagel condensation over N-doped carbon
case.protocol: Benzaldehyde (5.0 mmol, 1.0 equiv) and malononitrile (5.0 mmol, 1.0 equiv) were combined with an N-doped carbon heterogeneous basic catalyst in acetonitrile. The suspension was heated at 50 C for 24 h in a 25 mL round-bottom flask. The 2-benzylidenemalononitrile product was obtained in 85% yield.

analogies.summary: This Knoevenagel condensation reaction was successfully translated from batch to continuous flow processing using a glass chromatography column reactor. The reaction proceeded via nucleophilic addition followed by dehydration at room temperature (25°C) with a residence time of 9 minutes and flow rate of 1.5 mL/min at 0.25 M concentration. The flow process achieved a 99% yield compared to 95.2% in the batch baseline, representing a 3.8 percentage point improvement. The enhanced performance in flow was achieved while significantly reducing reaction time from 10 minutes in batch to just 9 minutes residence time, demonstrating both improved efficiency and yield in the continuous process.

optimization_table.key_findings: Flow rate of 1.5 mL/min and 95% EtOH solvent provided best yield and conversion.

metadata.mechanism_type: Lewis Acid Activation and Nucleophilic Attack

analogies.summary: This work describes a Knoevenagel condensation reaction using surface-immobilized ZnNx sites as Lewis acid catalysts. The reaction proceeds through Lewis acid activation followed by nucleophilic attack in aqueous solvent. Under flow conditions, the process achieved 99% yield with a 60-minute residence time at 0.1 mL/min flow rate using 0.2 M substrate concentration at room temperature. The flow setup utilized a back pressure regulator at 1.0 bar and operated in single-phase liquid regime. Flow chemistry enabled the reaction to proceed at room temperature while maintaining excellent yields, whereas the batch process required heating to 200°C, demonstrating significant energy savings and process intensification through improved heat and mass transfer in the continuous flow reactor.

analogies.summary: This process involves stilbene ester synthesis via nucleophilic addition-elimination mechanism using sodium methoxide as the base in methanol solvent. The reaction was conducted in a T-shaped borosilicate glass microreactor with electroosmotic flow (EOF) pumping at a flow rate of 0.4 mL/min and 20-minute residence time. The flow process achieved a 70% yield compared to 60% in batch under similar conditions (20-minute reaction time in methanol). The microreactor setup provided improved mixing and heat transfer compared to batch processing, resulting in a 10 percentage point yield improvement. The single-phase liquid operation in the microreactor enabled better control over reaction conditions and more efficient mass transfer.

chemistry.scope_summary: The study demonstrates the synthesis of a series of nitrostilbene esters using micro reactor technology, with varied reaction efficiencies depending on aldehyde substrates. The micro reactors produced yields of up to 70% under optimized conditions and showed potential for automated synthesis and analogue chemistry.

optimization_table.key_findings: Using an optimum pumping voltage of 400 V resulted in a well-controlled flow condition and higher yield.

Purge reactor with solvent to remove air if oxygen sensitivity is a concern (though Plan says not required).

proposal.chemistry_notes: Reaction is a Knoevenagel condensation using a heterogeneous N-doped carbon catalyst. Batch uses a suspension; flow translation requires a packed bed reactor to retain the solid catalyst. Analogy 1 used a glass chromatography column for a similar Knoevenagel reaction, supporting the packed bed approach. Residence time is significantly reduced from 24 h (batch) to 144 min (flow) based on kinetic intensification factors. Temperature remains at 50 C. No BPR required as T < bp - 20 C. Single liquid stream feeds the packed bed.
